patient.name: Mr. Elias Wisozk
patient.visitTitle: General adult exam — new hypertension and metabolic syndrome
patient.clinic: GREATER LAWRENCE FAMILY HEALTH CENTER INC

cases.rationale: Mr. Wisozk was newly started on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily for essential hypertension. Per the 2020 FDA labeling change, hydrochlorothiazide carries an increased risk of non-melanoma skin cancer, and patients should receive sun-protection counseling and routine skin examinations. Neither the visit note nor the transcript documents any sun-protection or skin-cancer counseling — the clinician counseled only on diuresis, orthostatic symptoms, cramping, and electrolytes. This is a genuine counseling gap for a patient beginning long-term thiazide therapy, but it is not urgent (no reported skin lesions or heightened risk factors documented), so medium priority is appropriate.
cases.draftedAction: For Mr. Elias Wisozk, counsel on sun protection (protective clothing, broad-spectrum sunscreen, limiting UV exposure) while taking hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, recommend routine skin examination given the FDA-labeled increased risk of non-melanoma skin cancer with hydrochlorothiazide, and document shared decision-making with Dr. Okafor. This counseling can be added at the already-scheduled 1-month blood pressure recheck.

cases.rationale: Mr. Howell was newly started on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily at this visit. FDA labeling changes (2020-08-20) describe increased non-melanoma skin cancer risk with hydrochlorothiazide and recommend sun protection counseling and regular skin examinations. This is especially relevant here: he is an 85-year-old man who reports frequent outdoor activity (daily walks and regular gardening), increasing cumulative sun exposure. Neither the transcript nor the visit note documents any skin-cancer risk counseling, sun-protection advice, or plan for routine skin examination, so the required monitoring is missing.
cases.draftedAction: For Mr. Isreal Delbert Howell, counsel on sun protection (broad-spectrum sunscreen, protective clothing/hat, limiting midday sun during morning walks and gardening) while taking Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG Oral Tablet, recommend routine skin examination with periodic full-body skin checks given the FDA-labeled increased non-melanoma skin cancer risk, and document shared decision-making with the prescribing physician. Add skin-cancer surveillance to the 6-month follow-up plan.

patient.name: Mr. Julius Alphonso Renner
patient.visitTitle: General exam — hypertension treatment initiation and chronic low back pain

cases.rationale: Mr. Renner was newly started on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily at this visit. Per the 2020 FDA labeling change, HCTZ carries an increased risk of non-melanoma skin cancer, and patients should be counseled on sun protection and routine skin examination. The transcript shows counseling covered dizziness, cough, and ankle swelling, but no sun-protection or skin-cancer screening counseling was provided or documented. This is a counseling/monitoring gap for a newly initiated therapy rather than an acute safety issue, so priority is low, but action is warranted.
cases.transcriptEscalation: No sun-protection or skin-examination counseling was documented during the visit despite new HCTZ initiation; recommend adding this counseling at or before the planned 4-6 week follow-up.
